items.followUp: State the two conditions required for rotational and translational equilibrium.

rubric.why: This is the condition for translational equilibrium.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for stating that the resultant force (net force) on the body is zero.

rubric.why: This is the condition for rotational equilibrium.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for stating that the resultant torque (moment) on the body is zero.

modelAnswer: The resultant force acting on a body must be zero (translational equilibrium).
The resultant torque acting on a body must be zero (rotational equilibrium).

items.followUp: A 2 kg object moves at 10 m s⁻¹. Calculate its kinetic energy.

rubric.why: The mass must be converted to kilograms and the kinetic-energy relation identified.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for using m = 0.5 kg and KE = ½mv².

rubric.why: This is the correctly calculated kinetic energy with its unit.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the answer 56.25 J.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 500 g = 0.5 kg, v = 15 m s⁻¹
Formula: K.E. = ½mv²
Substitution: K.E. = ½ × 0.5 kg × (15 m s⁻¹)²

items.followUp: What happens to the speed and kinetic energy of gas molecules when a gas is cooled?

rubric.why: Heating raises the molecules' average kinetic energy and speed.
rubric.description: Increase in kinetic energy or speed
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for stating that heating increases molecular kinetic energy or makes the molecules move faster.

rubric.why: Faster molecules move about more rapidly and collide more frequently.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for a further correct effect, such as more frequent collisions or faster movement through the gas.

modelAnswer: Heating increases the kinetic energy of gas molecules.

items.followUp: Draw the speed-time graph for a body moving with uniform deceleration and use it to obtain the relation v = u − at.

rubric.why: A uniform-acceleration speed-time graph is a straight line between the initial and final speeds.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for a straight-line speed-time graph labelled with speed and time, showing initial speed vi at t = 0 and final speed vf at time t.

rubric.why: The graph's gradient gives acceleration.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for identifying the gradient as (vf − vi)/t.

rubric.why: This states the definition of uniform acceleration in terms of the graph's gradient.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for equating acceleration a to the gradient or change in speed divided by time.

rubric.why: Rearranging the acceleration relation gives the required equation of motion.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for obtaining vf = vi + at.

modelAnswer: Draw time t on the horizontal axis and speed v on the vertical axis.
Mark the initial point (0, vi) and the final point (t, vf), then join them with a straight line for uniform acceleration.
Gradient of the speed-time graph = (vf − vi)/t.
For uniform acceleration, a = (vf − vi)/t.
Therefore, at = vf − vi.
Hence, vf = vi + at.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and derive the relation K.E. = ½mv² for a body starting from rest.

rubric.why: This is the definition of kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for defining kinetic energy as the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.

rubric.why: Work done on the body is used to obtain its kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for relating work to force and displacement, and force to mass and acceleration.

rubric.why: The kinematic relation provides the displacement needed in the work expression.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for using v² = u² + 2as (or its rearrangement) and taking u = 0 for a body starting from rest.

rubric.why: This is the required result after substituting the motion relation into work.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for deriving or stating K.E. = ½mv².

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
Work done, W = Fs, and F = ma.
For a body starting from rest, u = 0 and v² = u² + 2as, so s = v²/(2a).
W = Fs = ma × v²/(2a) = ½mv².
Therefore, K.E. = ½mv².
